description:
Map a job title in the user's own words to the occupation JobJump files it under, and optionally describe that occupation. Use it when the user's wording is unusual, colloquial, English or gendered and you want the canonical German occupation name, the other titles that mean the same job, or links to JobJump's salary, job-search and CV-template pages for it; and when the user asks what the job involves, what it requires, or how to write a CV for it. Give the title in `job_title`; the server normalises German gendered forms.

The result names the occupation as JobJump stores it, the four-digit KldB 2010 group code where JobJump maps one, up to 30 sibling titles with the total count, and up to 3 common alternative names that currently have postings on JobJump. search_jobs already matches every sibling title when given any one of them, so you do not need to search each alias separately.

Pass `include: ["profile"]` for JobJump's occupation profile (description, FAQs, typical skills, requirements, benefits, tags) and `include: ["cv_guidance"]` for the advice from JobJump's CV template (tips, common mistakes, key sections, featured skills, FAQs and the template link). Ask only for what the user needs; both are editorial content about the occupation in general. The profile leaves out sentences and FAQs about pay; use get_salary_benchmark or get_tariff_pay for pay.

When the title cannot be matched, the result is a success with `resolved: null` and a note; ask the user for another wording. The tool returns no salary figures and no postings – call get_salary_benchmark or search_jobs for those, and get_tariff_pay for public-sector pay tables.

include.description: Extra sections to add. Omit for the short result. 'profile' adds JobJump's occupation profile: description, FAQs, typical skills, requirements, benefits and tags, with pay figures and third-party statistics left out. 'cv_guidance' adds the advice from JobJump's CV template for the occupation: tips, common mistakes, key sections, featured skills and FAQs.

job_title.description: Occupation or job title in the user's own words, German or English. Gendered German forms are normalised, e.g. 'Erzieherin' resolves like 'Erzieher'.

name: get_occupation

key_sections.description: Sections a CV for this occupation should contain.

url.description: JobJump CV template the guidance belongs to.

cv_guidance.description: Present only when include asks for 'cv_guidance'; null when JobJump has no published CV template for the occupation.

benefits.description: Benefits employers commonly offer in this occupation.

description.description: JobJump's description of the occupation as plain text.

mandatory.description: Whether JobJump marks the requirement as usually mandatory.

skills.description: Skills JobJump lists as typical for the occupation.

profile.description: Present only when include asks for 'profile'; null when JobJump has no published profile for the occupation.

as_of.description: Vintage or reference period as published: 'YYYY', 'YYYY-MM' or an ISO date.

basis.description: Whether amounts are gross, net, or not a money amount.

dataset.description: Name of the dataset, e.g. 'Entgeltatlas' or 'JobJump salary aggregate'.

estimated.description: True when JobJump modelled or derived the value rather than observing or receiving it.

label.description: Short English name of what this series measures.

license.description: Licence or terms of use that apply to redistributing this series.

methodology_url.description: Public page describing how the series is produced, or null.

population.description: Who or what is counted, e.g. 'full-time employees subject to social insurance'.

sample_size.description: Number of underlying observations where JobJump knows it, otherwise null.

series_id.description: Stable key that series and values in this response refer to.

statistic.description: The statistic these values are. Read this before calling a value a median, a percentile or a maximum.

unit.description: Unit of every value carrying this series_id.

cv_template_url.description: JobJump CV template for the occupation, or null when there is none.

jobs_url.description: JobJump job search for the occupation.

kldb_code.description: Four-digit group code of the German occupational classification KldB 2010 that JobJump maps this occupation to, or null when there is no mapping.

label.description: JobJump's canonical name for the occupation, as stored.

salary_url.description: JobJump salary page for the occupation, or null when JobJump has no salary data for it.

search_aliases.description: Common alternative names for the occupation that have live postings on JobJump.

series_id.description: Provenance entry of the occupation mapping and titles.

sibling_count.description: Total number of job titles in the occupation.

sibling_titles.description: Other job titles JobJump files under the same occupation, alphabetical. search_jobs matches all of them when given any one.

title: Get an occupation
